description: Define the portable defense-library contracts and boundaries
steps: Execution ownership: the Ralph worker implements only this task and hands off files and remaining work. The supervising assistant executes validation and owns passes. Do not run test suites, flash devices, change this ledger, or start another task. Acceptance criteria below are for the supervising reviewer; if validation exposes a defect, revise this task before proceeding.

Separate packet acquisition, parser/detector adapters, evidence/business logic, presentation and board drivers. Core headers use standard C++ types only; no Arduino, ESP-IDF, M5Stack, graphics, filesystem or network dependencies. Inject monotonic time and typed observations.

Define board/radio capabilities for supported bands/channels, display geometry, input controls, BLE, memory and storage. Never hardcode StickS3 pins, 2.4 GHz-only channels, PSRAM or a display into the defense core. A headless adapter runs the same logic; optional features report unsupported explicitly.

Use native ESP-IDF initially. Zephyr now has a StickS3 board target; evaluate it on actual raw-radio integration and resource costs, not a false claim that board support is missing. Keep OS-specific queue/driver behavior behind adapters.

Deliver typed contracts for raw receive metadata, bounded frame input, parser results, normalized AP settings, incidents, monotonic time/epoch, freshness/coverage and board/radio capabilities. Reuse existing core/presenter types where sound. Keep UI drawing, device pins and OS queues outside the defense library. Document ownership, byte identity, capacity limits and error/unknown semantics.

Deliver a dependency diagram and API examples for headless replay and a later ESP-IDF adapter. This task is contracts and boundaries, not hardware bring-up, a parser rewrite or full detector implementation.

Reviewer acceptance: inspect the public headers and dependency graph for SDK/display isolation, explicit unsupported capabilities and implementable ownership/lifetime rules. Confirm existing code migration is described. Hardware and cross-target builds are later gates.

Implement a documented v1 rating of advertised Wi-Fi configuration, not a probability of being hacked: Very good = WPA3-Personal SAE-only with supported CCMP/GCMP and PMF required; Good = WPA2-Personal only with CCMP and PMF required; Medium = WPA2-Personal with CCMP and PMF optional or disabled, or valid WPA2/WPA3 transition with supported strong ciphers; Bad = original WPA or any advertised TKIP option; Horrible = unencrypted open access or WEP. Apply the weakest advertised supported mode, so a legacy fallback cannot earn a high rating.

Treat the mood mapping as our documented product policy, not a standard certification. Transition mode is a valid compatibility choice. Show the exact PMF limitation and advice rather than calling every WPA2 network broken. Unknown options prevent a complete grade; retain any separately confirmed legacy-risk finding. Check both group and pairwise ciphers, every AKM, and PMF consistency. Do not infer actual client negotiation or authenticated AP identity from spoofable advertisements.

Treat OWE, Enterprise modes, inconsistent settings and unparsed security fields as unsupported/unknown until their policies are deliberately specified. Do not call all privacy-bit-clear networks unencrypted: check OWE. Unknown is an observation overlay, not a sixth rated mood. Show 'Checking' at startup and 'No fresh data' after 30 seconds without a usable sample; never leave a stale happy rating looking current.

Use docs/research/wifi-audit.md as the source-audit baseline. Each reading must retain source, SSID bytes, BSSID, monotonic observation time, channel and parsing status. Independent RSSI/receive activity must not refresh expired security evidence; after reboot cached settings are historical until observed again.

Test core isolation using wrong BSSID, same SSID on another AP, binary/hidden SSIDs, delayed/future timestamps, reboot/timebase changes, expired evidence, malformed newer samples, queue drops and demo/imported/live origin separation. Future timestamps must not poison all later live observations.

Keep selection identity and rating in portable code. Raw RSSI/activity does not renew security evidence; malformed newer samples, clock epochs and unknown options must not create a fresh positive grade. Preserve demo/imported/live separation.

Reviewer acceptance: execute fixtures for all five moods, unknown/OWE/Enterprise cases, cipher combinations, PMF consistency, duplicate SSIDs, delayed/future samples, reboot and stale timeout. No networking, display, password knowledge or device boot is required to pass this library task.

Count deauthentication/disassociation observations within documented time windows and actual listening coverage. Handle retry deduplication without assuming sequence numbers uniquely identify an event. For protected frames distinguish observable headers from encrypted bodies; never read an encrypted reason code or claim MIC verification without the required keys.

Treat thresholds as tunable heuristics, document cooldowns, and display the observed count/window and uncertainty. Normal reconnects, roaming, AP reboot, repeated frames and short listening gaps must be part of calibration. A burst means observed disconnect traffic, not proof clients were disconnected or an attacker identified.

Use explicit baseline approval; do not silently learn trust from nearby packets. Same SSID with another BSSID, changed channel, RSSI changes or deauth followed by EAPOL can warrant investigation but cannot alone confirm an evil twin, a named attack tool, or a passive sniffer. Approved mesh/extender APs must be handled normally.

Implement bounded detector state, configurable time windows and explicit approved-AP baselines behind G01 contracts. Prepare fixture/replay cases for benign roaming, reconnects, retries, sequence wrap, protected/malformed frames, bursts and coverage gaps.

Reviewer acceptance: execute these cases and inspect count/window/uncertainty outputs and bounded resource use. Record replay-only confidence. Physical false-positive calibration remains a separate requirement of G13; do not claim hardware effectiveness here.

The owner's own StickS3 firmware ~/dev/m5/sticks3-ai-usage (firmware/src/hal/sticks3/power.cpp, docs/DEVICES.md; ptt.ino lineage, each write a measured leak fix): ext1 wake on the buttons GPIO11/GPIO12 active low; teardown = display sleep, LCD rail off (PM1 GPIO2), PA off (PM1 GPIO3), ES8311 codec low power (I2C 0x18: 0x0D<-0xFC, 0x0E<-0x6A, 0x00<-0x00), BMI270 suspend (0x68: 0x7D<-0x00, 0x7C<-0x03); never arm the PM1 IRQ wake (GPIO1->GPIO13: conflicts with SDA and hangs PM1 I2C after wake); never deep-sleep on USB power (VBUS > 4000 mV, debounced); 250 mAh cell, deep sleep with button wake measured at weeks of standby.

Power states, SDK-free and host-tested (for example adapters/power/idle.{hpp,cpp}): Active (normal screens and motion). Dim after power.dim_s (TUNE, default 30 s) without motion (G16A IMU), key press or ALERT: backlight to a low TUNE level, reduced frame rate, a minimal symbol view (rating glyph and mood colour, honest no-data/ALERT states kept); passive monitoring continues; motion, a key or a new ALERT returns to Active. Deep sleep after power.sleep_s (TUNE, default 120 s) more without activity, only on battery: show 'sleeping - press to wake' about 1 s, stop the radio, run the teardown above, arm ext1 ANY_LOW on GPIO11|GPIO12, enter deep sleep; no timer wake, no IMU wake. Never sleep on USB power, during UPDATE or a TUNE session, while an ALERT is shown, or during onboarding.

Wake: a press of either key boots the Guardian; that press is swallowed (never a UI action). After wake the screen honestly shows that nothing was observed while asleep (searching / no fresh data until a new observation), exactly like a cold boot. STATUS adds power_state=, wake_cause=, sleep_count= (RTC-retained) and the time spent asleep.

Source of ideas: AntiHunter (~/dev/AntiHunter, commit c6ef921) is AGPL-3.0-only: copy NO code; re-implement independently from the behaviour described here, keep its constants only as uncalibrated hypotheses (policy of docs/research/reuse-decisions.md). Never transmit, never name an attack tool, never claim compromise: observations with count/window/uncertainty ('seen nearby', 'on your network').

Implement each as an independent FrameDetector (bounded tables, O(1) per frame, cooldown, area scope unless it concerns the selected network), with AntiHunter's behaviour as the starting hypothesis (all values TUNE): (1) Probe flood: randomized-source flood (>=80 probe requests and >=60 distinct sources in 5 s), single-source flood (>=60 per 5 s in 2 consecutive windows), per-SSID flood (>=40 distinct sources asking for one SSID in 5 s); 60 s quiet before re-alert; ignore random-looking SSIDs only as a documented rule. (2) Beacon flood: >=40 distinct BSSIDs at >= -65 dBm within 10 s (RSSI gate prevents far-away false positives); while active, suppress per-beacon noise. (3) Karma/MANA responder (passive half only, no bait): one transmitter answering for >=N distinct SSIDs via probe responses/beacons within 60 s, excluding Multi-BSSID APs; stronger when the answered SSIDs match recently observed probe requests. (4) Auth flood: per BSSID >=16 distinct sources and >=60 open-system auth frames in 5 s. (5) SAE commit flood (Dragonblood-style DoS): per BSSID SAE commits minus confirms >=10 in 5 s. (6) Assoc-sleep: per BSSID >=8 (re)assoc requests with the power-management bit or >=4 distinct sources in 5 s. (7) CSA/Quiet abuse: CSA switch count >=50 or a CSA from the selected BSSID that its own beacons never announced; Quiet duration >=1000 TU; 30 s per BSSID. (8) SSID confusion (CVE-2023-52424): probe response SSID differs from that BSSID's beacon SSID (hidden NUL-SSID handled, not a mismatch). (9) Pwnagotchi nearby: beacon from DE:AD:BE:EF:DE:AD or with vendor element 222; one alert per 30 s per BSSID. (10) OWE transition abuse: an open beacon reusing an OWE AP's SSID that is not its declared partner.
